research_rationale:
EO 13792 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act, signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13792.txt, OCR text layer of three PDF pages; page images were not inspected and requires_page_check is false). Operative content: Sec. 1 policy; Sec. 2(a)-(c) Secretary of the Interior review of monument designations, factors and consultation; Sec. 2(d)-(e) interim report in 45 days and final report in 120 days (report deadlines, never ends); Sec. 3 general provisions. It has no sunset and no own-terms ending. The first and only end found is Sec. 7(a) of EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037; held official text, Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 read in full): 'Executive Order 13792 of April 26, 2017 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act) ... are hereby revoked.' The revocation of EO 13792 is unconditional (the exception wording in Sec. 7 concerns only EO 13834, EO 13920 and memoranda) and EO 13990 states no delayed effective date, so it took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR catalog: 2 hits, both EO 13990, no reinstatement candidate) were read and carry no coverage warning; they show no earlier ending and no later revival. Judgment on performance: the Secretary's review and reports ordered by Sec. 2 may have been completed in 2017, but no held source dates them, a report deadline is not an end and the order is not self-terminating, so the order is treated as operative until revoked on 2021-01-20. The independent reviewer should test that judgment.

savings.reason: EO 13990 Sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13792 with no saving clause; Sec. 7(f) directs OMB and agencies to rescind implementing actions (a wind-down, not a saving); EO 13792 Sec. 3(c) creates no rights; any later monument proclamation is a separate Presidential instrument. No residual command found in the held EO 13990 text or the three machine searches.
